name: Search Relevance Service
tagline: A standalone ranking service that took relevance tuning out of a monolith and into something product could iterate on weekly.

seo.title: Search Relevance Service — Martin Zachariassen
seo.description: A standalone ranking service that took relevance tuning out of a monolith, built in Kotlin and Elasticsearch.

cover.alt: Diagram of a search request flowing through a scoring step driven by a published config version, split across an A/B variant, into ranked results.
cover.caption: A ranking change is a config publish, not a deploy.

summary: Ranking logic lived inline in the search endpoint of the main monolith, so every relevance change needed a full deploy and a release owner. I extracted it into its own gRPC service with a config-driven scoring pipeline, so product and search specialists could ship ranking changes without engineering in the loop.

blocks.value: The new service reads a versioned scoring config at request time, so a ranking change is a config publish rather than a deploy. Every request also logs which config version scored it, which made the A/B rollout of new ranking strategies straightforward to attribute.
